accepted_concepts.summary: NES Sprite 0/MMC3 raster concepts are useful only as historical analogy; Mega Drive implementation must be expressed through VDP HSCROLL_LINE/HSCROLL_TILE/WINDOW/H-Int/plane ownership.
Parallax depth can come from bands or lines inside a plane, not only separate BG_A/BG_B layers; composition must declare scanline bands, ratios, horizon and fallback.
Pseudo-3D road/floor effects require horizon line, per-line ratio curve or LUT, camera source, transfer method, update cadence and cheaper fallback.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: NES Sprite 0 hit or mapper IRQ workflow should be copied as Mega Drive architecture
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. The Mega Drive has different VDP mechanisms; NES details are historical background, not implementation rules.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: Line scroll creates unlimited independent background layers
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. It distorts or offsets one plane by row/line; it does not create new planes or independent tilemaps.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: The illustrative demo proves a ready runtime road/parallax engine
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. It lacks budget, art authoring contract, camera/input ownership, fallback and emulator evidence.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: A linear proximity formula is sufficient for all pseudo-3D roads
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. The curve must be authored and verified against the actual art, camera speed and gameplay readability.

required_followups_before_production: hscroll table ownership and update timing
formula or LUT for line offsets
per_frame_dma_budget_report or equivalent VDP budget review
camera behavior contract when the effect follows gameplay camera
art authoring check for band/line readability
BlastEm evidence for runtime motion claims
